items.title: Section: Eight Circumstances Where the Dharma Simply Cannot Be Heard

items.zh: 根者，亦略有二種。謂順淨分及順不淨分。如根，如是界、信解、意樂，當知亦爾。此中差別者，根是果性，界是因性，信解是因性，意樂是果性。隨眠者，亦略有二種。謂可害及非可害。生者，亦略有二種。謂無暇生及有暇生。
items.en: Faculty is, briefly, of two kinds: according with purity and according with impurity. Element, faith and understanding, and aspiration should be known in just the same way. The difference among these is that faculty is the fruit, element is the cause, faith and understanding is the cause, and aspiration is the fruit. Latent tendency is, briefly, of two kinds: destructible and indestructible. Rebirth is, briefly, of two kinds: inopportune rebirth and opportune rebirth.

items.zh: 習氣者，亦有二種。謂無間生習氣及前生習氣。聚者，有三種。一、邪性定聚，二、正性定聚，三、不定聚。

items.title: Section: Wrongly Fixed, Rightly Fixed, and Undecided — Three Groupings Complete the Thirteen

items.zh: 邪性定聚復有二種。一、本性邪性定，二、方便邪性定。正性定亦有二種。一、本性正性定，二、方便正性定。不定亦有二種。一、本性不定，二、方便不定。
items.en: Wrongly fixed grouping is also of two kinds: inherently wrongly fixed, and wrongly fixed through acquired means. Rightly fixed grouping is also of two kinds: inherently rightly fixed, and rightly fixed through acquired means. Indeterminate grouping is also of two kinds: inherently indeterminate, and indeterminate through acquired means.

items.zh: 復次，由造作等十三種法，應知廣說十三種補特伽羅，如其所應。問：若有善造作，彼一切不善造作不相應耶？設不善造作不相應，彼一切有善造作耶？答：應作四句。或有善造作，非不善造作不相應。謂諸能造黑白黑白異熟業者所有善造作。或有不善造作不相應，非善造作，謂無記造作。或有善造作，亦不善造作不相應，謂能造作白白異熟業，及不黑不白異熟業，能盡諸業者所有造作。或有非善造作，亦非不善造作不相應。謂能造作黑黑異熟業者所有造作。如是不善造作、無記造作，如其所應盡當知。問：若成就業障，亦成就習氣障耶？設成就習氣障，亦成就業障耶？答：應作四句。或有成就業障，非習氣障。謂如有一，於現法中，於五無間業亦作亦增長；於前生中，於此種類惡不善業不作不增長；彼現法中能障聖道。或有成就習氣障，非業障。謂與此相違。或有俱成就。謂於現法中，於五無間業亦作亦增長；於前生中，於此種類惡不善業亦作亦增長；彼現法中能障聖道。或有俱不成就。謂與此相違。

items.title: Section: Three Natures Open the Deepest Truth of All

items.zh: 云何非安立真實？謂諸法真如圓成實自性，聖智所行、聖智境界、聖智所緣。云何增益邊？謂諸法自性略有三種。一、遍計所執自性，二、依他起自性，三、圓成實自性。遍計所執自性者，謂諸所有名言安立諸法自性，依假名言，數數周遍計度諸法而建立故。依他起自性者，謂眾緣生他力所起諸法自性，非自然有，故說無性。
items.en: What is non-established truth? The very suchness and perfected nature of all phenomena, the domain, object, and support of noble wisdom alone. What is the extreme of exaggeration? The self-nature of phenomena is, briefly, of three kinds: the imagined nature, the dependent nature, and the perfected nature. The imagined nature is whatever self-nature of phenomena is established through name and convention, repeatedly and pervasively conceived and constructed on the basis of assumed names. The dependent nature is the self-nature of phenomena arising through many conditions and through the power of other things, not existing of its own accord, and so said to be without self-nature.

items.title: Section: A Dream, a Dreamer, and Waking Up to Find Nothing There

items.zh: 圓成實自性者，謂如前說。若於依他起自性、或圓成實自性中，所有遍計所執自性妄執，當知名增益邊。所以者何？此自性中，彼自性有不應理故。此不應理，如菩薩地已略顯示，彼決擇中當廣分別。又若略說，由三因緣不應道理。謂種種非一品類名言所安立故；若離名言，彼覺不生故；又彼名言依義轉故。
items.en: The perfected nature is as already explained: the suchness of all phenomena, the domain, object, and support of noble wisdom, able to bring about the realisation of purity, liberation from every bond of characteristics and afflictive residue, and to draw forth every excellent quality. Within these natures, the dependent and the perfected, the assumption of that other, imagined nature does not accord with reason. Briefly stated, this is so for three reasons: because such things are established through varied and non-uniform names; because, apart from a name, no cognition of the thing would arise; and because names themselves follow upon meaning already present.

items.title: Section: Beyond Mere Words — What the Special Meaning Actually Points To

items.zh: 損減邊者，謂於依他起自性及圓成實自性諸有法中，謗其自相，言無所有。
items.en: The extreme of diminishment is slandering the very own-characteristic of the dependent nature and the perfected nature among all existing phenomena, saying that they do not exist at all. Answer: the intention of special meaning is not the meaning corresponding merely to the names, phrases, and letters of the teaching, but is understood only by setting aside such words and penetrating to the further ultimate meaning they point towards.

blocks.text: The three natures, illustrated by a dream: waking, one finds nothing was there.
Faculty is fruit, disposition is cause; faith and understanding are cause, aspiration fruit.

Master Cháng Bǎi: though one may have a vehicle's lineage, committing the five grave deeds is being "fixed in wrongness". (Untranslated, 0656b07: a long four-case analysis: one may make wholesome karma yet not be free of the unwholesome; one may have the obstruction of karma without the obstruction of habit, or the reverse, or both; for example, committing a heinous deed in this life without such habits from past lives.)
The imagined nature is whatever is set up through name and convention, conceived again and again on borrowed names.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the dependent and perfected natures are by nature beyond words; adding a verbal self-nature to them does not accord with reality.
Master Cháng Bǎi stresses the letters that compose names and phrases.
The dream is the treatise's favourite image for the imagined nature: vivid while it lasts, nothing there on waking.

quiz.q: After faculty as fruit and realm as cause, what are faith and understanding and aspiration?
options: faith and understanding is the fruit and aspiration the cause
faith and understanding is the cause, and aspiration is the fruit
both are the cause
both are the fruit
quiz.why: The treatise says faculty is the fruit, realm the cause, faith and understanding the cause, and aspiration the fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that with understanding one gladly acts, so understanding is cause and aspiration fruit.

quiz.q: 界 in "realm is the cause" is rendered realm. Why is this a poor choice?
options: 界 here is causal, like disposition; realm is easily confused with the desire realm and so on
nothing: this 界 is the desire, form, and formless realms, the cause of birth and death
it should be world
it should be fruit
quiz.why: The treatise calls 界 causal, listing it with faith and understanding, so it means a being's disposition. In this English the word realm usually means the desire realm and the like, so element or disposition would be clearer.

quiz.q: 方便邪性定 is rendered "circumstantially wrongly fixed." What is inexact?
options: nothing: 方便 means chance conditions, one happening upon a situation with no action of one's own involved
it should be inherently
it should be rightly fixed
方便 means brought about by action, like the five grave deeds, not by circumstance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though one may have a vehicle's lineage, committing the five grave deeds or the like is called fixed in wrongness through 方便. The rightly fixed version likewise means entering the path, so action decides it rather than circumstance.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define the imagined nature?
options: the self-nature of what arises through conditions and others' power, false because dependent
the self-nature set up by names, repeatedly and pervasively conceived on the basis of assumed names
suchness, the domain of noble wisdom
the Great Lord taught by other paths
quiz.why: The treatise says the imagined nature is whatever is established through name and convention, repeatedly conceived on the basis of assumed names. Arising through conditions defines the dependent nature, which is a distinct nature.

quiz.q: "Within this nature, the assumption of that other, imagined nature...." What is wrong with this nature?
options: it should mean both the dependent and perfected natures; a gap makes it point to the perfected alone
nothing: it means the perfected nature alone, since the dependent nature does contain the imagined
彼自性 should be the perfected nature
此自性 should be the imagined nature
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: both of these are by nature apart from words, and to add a verbal self-nature to the dependent or perfected nature does not accord with reason. A missing sentence leaves the English pointing to the perfected nature alone.

quiz.q: 名身、句身、文身 is rendered "words, phrases, and sentences" in section 47. What is off?
options: nothing: 文身 means a composition, a full sentence, and it is section 68's letter that is wrong and should become sentences
文身 means letters, not sentences; section 68 has name, phrase, and letter
it should be verses, chapters, and books
it should be sounds, tones, and rhythms
quiz.why: 文身 are the letters that compose names and phrases. Sections 47 and 68 render the same term differently, and section 68 is right. Master Cháng Bǎi stresses removing attachment to a verbal self-nature in the words themselves.
